What makes the egret so amazing?

The graceful egret of rice paddies and waterside is a waterbird you can spot at a glance by its snow-white feathers and long legs. And it's a very patient hunter!

content.alt: Egret - Nature and science facts about the egret
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the egret

The egret steps lightly through shallow water on its long legs and catches fish, frogs, and insects with its long neck and pointed beak. When it hunts, it's a patient hunter that stays perfectly still for a long time, then plunges its beak down like lightning the moment prey comes near. Its snow-white feathers stand out by the water, so it often appeared in old Korean paintings and poems, and in spring and summer egrets gather in groups to build nests in trees and raise their chicks.

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Try connecting "If you move, the fish swim away, so you have to wait" to a "freeze" game like Statues. Watching an egret at a rice paddy or waterside lets your child see the patient hunt firsthand.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why does the egret wait perfectly still?
A. Because if it moves, the fish swim away. When prey comes close, it plunges its beak down like lightning to catch it.

Q. Where do egrets live?
A. By rivers, rice paddies, and waterside. In spring and summer they gather in groups to build nests in trees and raise their chicks.

Q. How can we observe it at home?
A. Connect it to a "freeze" game, and watch the patient hunt at a rice paddy or waterside.
